Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live''

RETRACTOR, ABDOMINAL, MORRIS' PATTERN 



1. Scope — Dimensional and t)ther requirements of Morris' pattern abdominal retractor used fn 
general surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

FIG. 1 RETRACTOR, ABDOMINAL, MORRIS' PATTERN 

2.1 A deviation of ± 2*5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

3. Material — Stainless ^teel conforming to Designation 20Cr13 or 30Cr13 of 18:6603-1972 

' Specification for stainless steel bars and flats \ 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The retractor shall be well and evenly finished. 

4.2 The retractor shall befreelrom any burrs, pits, cracl^s and other surface defects. 

4.3 The edges of the blade shall be properly rounded. 

4.4 The retractor shall be polished bright and passivated. 

5. Heat Treatment — The retractor shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 880 to 
430 HV.

6. Tests 

6.1 Rigidity Test 

6.1.1 The retracting part of the blade shall be applied to the edge of a chair or table. It shall be 
pulled manually by exerting a maximum force along the axis of the handle. The retractor shall 
show no sign of damage or permanent set. 

6.1.2 A load of 25 kg shall be suspended from the top of the turned end of the retracting blade. 
The maximum load shall be gradually attained and maintained for 2 minutes. On completion of 
the test the retractor shall show no sign of damage. 

6.2 Corrosion Resistance — The retractor shall satisfy the boilinrg and autoclaving test as mentioned 
in IS : 7531-1975 ' Boiling and autoclaving method o1 test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel 
surgical instruments. 

6.2.1 Subject to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier, the retractor may be put to the 
following test: 

Copper Sulpiiate Test — Scrub the sample with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water 
and then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the sample. Immerse in copper sulphate solution at 
room temperature for 6 minutes and wash off with fresh water or wet cotton wjooI. Composition of 
the solution shall be as follows: 

Copper sulphate ( CUSO4.5H2O ) 4'0 g 

Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) (spgr1"84) 10"0 g 

Distilled water [ see IS : 1070-1960 Specification 
for water, distilled quality ( revised) ] 90'0 ml 

No red stains or spots on the sample shall be allowed but dulling of the polished surface' 
may be permitted. 

7. Marking — Each retractor shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name^ initials or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) The words * Stainless Steel ', 

7.1 IS! Certification MarA/V7flf~ Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — Wrap each retractor in a moisture-proof paper or put in a polyethylene bag and pack 
in cardboard cartons. The retractor may also be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier.
